newsitem.title: UK: Mideast VLCCs buoyant on tight tonnage.
newsitem.headline: Mideast VLCCs buoyant on tight tonnage.

text.p: Very large crude carrier (VLCC) rates held firm on Tuesday on tight tonnage, with Mediterranean rates also resilient in an active market, brokers said. Mideast/Japan and South Korea VLCCs were fixed at around W70 with few vessels available up to at least mid-June, while Mideast/northwest Europe rates were steady at W57.5/60.
Typical in the Mideast/east sector was the 260,000 tonne Front Duchess, fixed Yanbu/South Korea at W70 for Ssangyong.
Current Mideast/Japan rates are well above the April average of W57.77 and the 1996 average of W61.64, according to figures on New York-based Rigos Chartering Inc's Internet site.
West Africa/U.S. Gulf rates also remained buoyant at W65, "or maybe a touch higher," one broker said. The 260,000 tonne World Champion proved his point, achieving W67.5 for Sohio.

The Mediterranean was active, with 130,000 tonne vessels (Suezmaxes) fixed at W95 and 80,000 tonners (Aframaxes) achieving W107.5. "The Aframax market has been quite busy and with W107.5 being done quite comfortably, I think rates may go up," one broker said.
Inter-U.K./Cont 80,000 tonne rates showed signs of slipping after dipping to W137.5 on Friday, almost 10 points down from their recent peak.
Brokers saw the current rate at about W117.5 on a lack of cargoes. "If we can stay at W110-115 it will not be too bad, but there is not enough activity in the north to be confident," one said.

North European fuel oil rates stayed firm at W245 for 25,000 tonnes, buoyed by seasonal Baltic exports and a great shortage of ships. Rates in the Med remained soft at around W195, but one broker said he expected these to rise, influenced by high U.K./Cont levels and pressure on larger, 50,000 tonne vessels.
Caribbean rates were steady, with 70,000 tonne crude cargoes fixed around W200 and 50,000 tonne fuel oil stems at W210/215.
